nm_mismatches.result: not a conversion or mass problem; a difference between the local inverse-dynamics re-run and the publisher's values
nm_mismatches.evidence: Local inverse_dynamics.sto vs published per-kg x mass (normal_walk_1): AB06, AB08, AB12 agree to 1e-5 to 1e-13 N*m. AB01 (kept, own mass 78.9, never rescaled) misses by 0.10 N*m (0.039% of peak), the same size as AB10 0.03 N*m (0.02%), AB05 0.03 N*m (0.016%) in my pass at the table mass (the worker reports up to 0.08 N*m over all columns). For AB01, AB05 and AB10 the least-squares divisor is exactly the table mass (78.9, 78.9, 84.1) and the residual with the best-fit mass equals the residual at the table mass, so the mass is right and what is left is shape noise from the re-run. AB09: fitted divisor 87.49-87.58 (table 87.6, audit slope 87.57), residual 0.09-0.37% of peak at either divisor; the same kind of difference, larger. The .sto prints 8 decimals, so rounding is not the cause. AB02 and AB03 .sto files do not match their normal_walk_1 published moments at all (nRows equal but residual ~90% of peak), and AB13 has 50002 rows vs 52903, so those are not alignable and not in the 7 exact set.
nm_mismatches.judgement: Acceptance wording 1e-3 N*m is too tight for a re-run; it fails for a kept recording too. The mass check holds at the level that matters (divisor to 5 significant figures for AB05, AB10; 0.03% for AB09). Treat the 3 misses as a limitation of the local re-run, recorded; nothing to change.
nm_mismatches.caveat: AB09 is the least tight (0.37% of peak at the worst column); its factor depends on the divisor 87.57-87.6, which differs by 0.03%.
